scope: canvas viewport pan, node drag appearance, low-zoom prompt rendering and transient overlays
rootCauses: Dense pan gestures replaced 332 real nodes with 144 coarse gray cards.
Node drag hid every non-active node content and the node header layer.
The moving flag was React state, so gesture start and end repainted the surface once.
At low zoom, 150 editable prompt cards made viewport pan write hundreds of culling attributes and repaint full editing DOM.
The function bar and creation panel subscribed to semantic store changes instead of subscribeDragging, so they stayed visible until a later node update.
fixes: Keep all React Flow node shells and real thumbnails mounted during gestures.
Pause imperative culling writes while the viewport moves and restore the 320px warm window after release.
Render low-zoom prompt cards in one world-space canvas snapshot during pan; images and all other nodes remain DOM.
Pause port hit-layer updates and hide its transient hit boxes during viewport motion.
Use subscribeDragging in the function bar and creation panel; hide both through data-viewport-moving during canvas pan or zoom.
Keep lightweight edge/background layers permanent and toggle visibility from native viewport attributes.
